title: LLM failures are cached as successful extraction results
reasoning: If an LLM call fails for one lot window, extract_lots logs a warning, continues, then writes lots_<id>.json. A later run treats that partial file as a valid cache and skips extraction entirely. Metadata has the same pattern: any extraction error becomes cached empty metadata. This can silently produce incomplete auction results that resume will not repair without manual cache invalidation.
recommendation: Track whether any extraction or metadata call failed and do not write the normal checkpoint unless the stage completed successfully. Either raise so batch mode records a failed item, or write an explicit incomplete/error artifact that resume does not treat as success.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: tests/test_extractor.py exercises parsing, merge, verification, and a happy-path extract_lots burst case, but it does not simulate a client.complete exception during a multi-window extraction or assert cache behavior after failure.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an extract_lots test with two windows and a mock client that raises on one window; assert the normal output_path is not written and the caller sees a failure or explicit incomplete status. Add a metadata test that a client failure does not write cached {} as a successful metadata file.
minimumFixScope: pipeline/extractor.py extract_lots and extract_metadata failure paths, plus focused tests in tests/test_extractor.py.
